scope: App/replay/training/CPU/private-network and buyable objects; partial findings are explicit. No hardware/human or final release-candidate acceptance claim.

findings.title: Regular CPU purchases techniques its policy does not deliberately execute
findings.implementation: One SupportsRental capability predicate filters both the CPU purchase pool and execution choices. All supported rentals receive deliberate ordinary-command policy inputs; unsupported air/field/branch-entry-only tools are excluded from purchases.
findings.limitations: 13 core / 17 expanded seeded art-or-rental witnesses. These prove intentional execution, not strong strategy or balanced prices.

findings.title: CPU super logic ignores actual selected-art affordability and Vale supers
findings.implementation: Both fighters select the current art definition and its actual cost. Shared encoder emits real motion/chord/charge samples; selected-art traces start with precisely that price and verify exactly one startup debit.
findings.limitations: No hidden competitive funding; each art witness is a separate training setup. Values are fixture evidence, not observed human play.

findings.title: Players cannot equip rentals through the reviewed training menus
findings.implementation: Two-seat training configuration/loadout menu, catalog TryMoveInLab, actual rental removal/reset, independent credits, legal demonstrations and single-action free-kit comparison. Active private sessions reject entering the lab.
findings.limitations: Normal-control visual walkthrough belongs to root native evidence. Comparison is move teaching, not an equal-opening-wallet rental experiment. Specific-item counter presets are simple class-based scripts plus exact tradeoff guidance.

findings.title: Regular CPU cannot meaningfully adapt to revealed equipment
findings.implementation: Immutable public loadout, selected-art, wallet and fighter observations are delayed by12 ticks. CPU adjusts throw avoidance for revealed command throws and defensive probability for actual opponent-art affordability.
findings.limitations: Bounded explicit strategies only; not a general learner. Opponent input and future simulation states are never exposed to policy.

findings.title: Link and hit-confirm drills can use weak success predicates
findings.implementation: Link progress requires continuous defender stun and a connected second normal after own recovery. Hit confirm requires the actual prior hit contact/action and accepted selected-super spend; gaps and blocks invalidate continuity.
findings.limitations: The measured close-MP to MK route replaces the old LP-to-LP false-positive fixture. Full human execution is separate.

findings.title: Advanced drills rely on generic sparring rather than precise practice feeds
findings.implementation: Advanced parry/red/multihit/quickrise feeds use deterministic legal commands with reachable reset spacing; feeds actually hit the neutral fixture. Checkpoints capture queued commands, dummy RNG, progress, recording and demonstration state.
findings.limitations: A learner still performs the defense. Air feed uses a vertical jump; no automatic successful parry is manufactured. Optimized per-item punish scripts are not claimed.

findings.title: Training lineup is constrained to the opposite character
findings.implementation: TrainingConfiguration independently specifies fighters, selected arts, wallets, equipment and stage for both seats. Reset preserves it; menus render authoritative IDs. Mirror lineup and all current action entrypoints are exercised.
findings.limitations: Palette selection remains presentation-owned; software evidence does not establish every controller menu path.

findings.title: Loading a replay from paused playback does not reset shell playback state
findings.implementation: StartReplay centralizes fresh playback state, accumulator, pause, input history, effects and timeline initialization. Every seek clears presentation state.
findings.limitations: Native replay-A pause/archive/replay-B walkthrough has not been recorded by this subtask.

findings.title: Results claim a replay was saved even after a save error
findings.implementation: SaveReplay returns ReplaySaveResult, parent result/Pause UI displays its actual Message. Failure retains the in-memory recorder. An economy-sidecar failure cannot falsely invalidate the saved replay.
findings.limitations: Locked destination exercises the real filesystem error path. Full-disk native UI fixture is not claimed.

findings.title: Archive sorts filenames and only exposes eight entries
findings.implementation: Archive metadata has UTC creation, unique ID, matchup and final-match completion. List sorts timestamp then stable path; shell pages all entries eight per page and labels incompatible/corrupt imports.
findings.limitations: No search/filter UI; pagination and native mixed-archive visual walkthrough are source-reviewed only.

findings.title: Replay corruption during playback needs a safe error boundary
findings.implementation: ReplayOperation wraps playback and seeking, preserves mismatch details, pauses and presents a safe error screen with archive/restart. Later command wallet tampering is rejected by replay verification.
findings.limitations: The production App throws at the exact bad command; graphical error-screen capture is separate.

findings.title: Replay persistence lacks collision-proof names and atomic replacement
findings.implementation: GUID/subsecond immutable filenames; sibling CreateNew temporary file, Flush(true), atomic same-filesystem rename and cleanup. Bounded64MiB streaming load prevents growth between initial stat and deserialization.
findings.limitations: Locked-file replacement and unique saves were executed. Sudden hardware power loss and all filesystems are not claimed.

findings.title: All presentation events wait for confirmed remote input
findings.implementation: Stable action/event IDs emit reversible local Add, then Confirm or Cancel after rollback. Spend, contact outcomes and terminal/settlement remain confirmed. Source fighter metadata is included in event identity for reflected projectiles.
findings.limitations: Rollback correction test verifies speculative startup cancellation and excludes unconfirmed economic/terminal outcomes. Physical button-to-speaker latency measurement is pending.

findings.title: Both peers must manually duplicate the entire lineup
findings.implementation: Optional private lobby agrees seat-owned fighter/art revisions plus host stage and a shared ready hash. Build/content/protocol validation precedes lobby. Shell uses this negotiated path; laboratory legacy complete-config path remains available.
findings.limitations: Executed on actual loopback sockets with differing initial lineup configs and asymmetric delay/loss/reordering. Two physical machines remain external.

findings.title: Some exit paths dispose the peer without sending disconnect
findings.implementation: Central LeavePrivateMatch plus Dispose best-effort reliable departure/ACK grace bounded250ms; socket failures become diagnostics and unconfirmed rounds never settle.
findings.limitations: Actual socket peer Dispose makes the other report Disconnected promptly. Physical pad removal and OS-forced process kill are separate checks.

findings.title: Pause/resume needs asymmetric-latency tests
findings.implementation: Host chooses a future pause tick beyond input delay/prediction, both advance neutral to matching confirmed hash, then pause. Resume requires the shared state and inserts120 neutral ticks; paused heartbeat prevents timeout.
findings.limitations: Asymmetric100/150ms, jitter20ms, loss3%, duplication/reordering and long healthy pause executed. Full combination of every terminal event with every timing offset is not claimed.

findings.title: Private rematch returns to connection setup
findings.implementation: Mutual in-session rematch retains the socket connection, requires matching completed state, changes match generation/session identity and resets wallets/plans/scores/input timelines. One-sided request cannot reset.
findings.limitations: Repeated same-lineup match is supported. Seat swaps and fighter/art changes still leave/reconnect through the lobby; no in-session postmatch re-selection protocol implemented.

findings.title: A compact in-game round economy ledger
findings.implementation: Replay format3 records canonical preparation and settlement receipts. RoundEconomyLedger reconstructs opening cash/rental/combat spend, nominal/granted/clipped payout, recovery tiers, closing cash and detailed debits with conservation assertions.
findings.limitations: Root owns in-game mini-ledger placement; export and actual full socket match ledger checked here. Historical format/build recordings remain incompatible and untouched.

findings.title: Private-session connection diagnostics and lobby quality
findings.implementation: Lobby ready/rematch/content compatibility and rollback/prediction diagnostics are available; fault lab records configured delay/loss/reorder and actual final states.
findings.limitations: No live measured RTT/jitter/loss estimator or public authentication claim. Injected fault percentages are laboratory configuration, not measurements of a live path.

findings.title: Economic telemetry should expose affordability and payout history rather than wallet totals alone
findings.implementation: Per-round actual receipt ledger exposes nominal/granted/clipped payout, prior/new recovery tier, all debits and opening/closing cash; parent purchase panel computes action capacity via canonical quote.
findings.limitations: Analytical continuing-state witnesses and price experiments are combat/BalanceLab ownership; no state-count enumeration is labeled a played match.

findings.title: Replay takeover for missed punish and spending decisions
findings.implementation: Replay controls open a detached TrainingSession.FromReplay. Core creates a training-bound snapshot retaining actual positions, wallet, leases, selected arts and current action; recording source stays unchanged.
findings.limitations: Core forbids restoring the training-bound snapshot into the competitive simulation; recorder rejects Training config. Demo test proves source hash/config remain immutable. Native takeover control-path capture is separate.

findings.title: Budget-aware combo and counterplay trials
findings.implementation: Legal catalog demonstrations and one-action free-kit comparisons use actual commands and debit receipts; existing confirm/link drills enforce real continuity.
findings.limitations: No complete authored free/EX/super route family from every same starter, nor optimized counter drill per rental. Current item-counter presets use class-based scripts and exact tradeoff guidance.

findings.title: Multi-slot dummy recordings and randomized defense
findings.implementation: Existing single dummy recording plus deterministic scripted modes retain checkpoints/RNG/playback/evaluator state.
findings.limitations: Multiple named recording slots, weighted playback, guard-after-first-hit and configurable wakeup/reversal menus remain optional follow-up work.

buyable_objects.implementation: Canonical unified projectile/field state; free normal-shot interactions, finite depth1 reflection, actual vertical Arc, Anchor arm/trigger/contact, Prism occupancy/collision/lifetime and owner interruption.
buyable_objects.interpretation: Reflection into an owner already holding an ordinary projectile dissipates the incoming shot, with no refund or transferred cost.
buyable_objects.future_extension: Current fighter restrictions prevent an armor-owner from owning a major field. A future combined fighter would require field interruption to inspect pre-arbitrated armor/KD results.

current_udp_matrix.scope: Actual two-process complete matches;0/50/100/150ms RTT, up to20ms jitter,3%loss,3%dup,10%reorder. Each pair verified final hash, wallets, scores, receipts and competitive replay.
current_udp_matrix.binding: Release development identity b1e682...; final ExportRelease rebinding awaits final actor-status cleanup and build.

final_candidate_binding: Superseded by user-requested shop-only-v2 migration. Preserve all pre-v2 evidence; no old direct-spend run is new-economy acceptance.
